metaTitle: Best Printers for College Students in 2026
metaDescription: Six printers for college students compared on dorm footprint, moving day, ink or toner cost, Wi-Fi and USB use, with picks for essays, labs and group projects.
expertTake: The Brother HL-L2405W is the best printer for most students because toner survives a summer in storage and each page costs very little. The Canon PIXMA TR4720 is the pick for students who also scan forms and need color occasionally. Anyone who prints under a dozen pages a semester should use the campus library and skip buying one.
introParagraphs: A student printer lives a hard life: it gets carried into a dorm, shares a desk with a laptop, sits idle over breaks and then has to produce a forty page paper at midnight before a deadline. Compact size, a forgiving paper path and low cost per page matter more than speed.

Choose by how you will really print. If most pages are black essays and readings, a small laser is cheapest and toughest. If you need color for posters and lab reports, an inkjet or ink tank covers it. Campus networks can also block printers, so a USB fallback is worth having.

products.name: Brother HL-L2405W Compact Wireless Mono Laser
products.description:
For a student who prints essays, syllabi and readings, this compact Brother laser is the sensible default. Toner stays usable through a summer in a closet, so the first page of the fall semester prints as sharply as the last page of spring, and the Brother Mobile Connect app handles printing from a phone.

What you give up is that it prints in black only and has no scanner. A student who needs color for a poster or a lab chart will visit the library for those pages, and the Canon PIXMA TR4720 handles them at home. There is no automatic duplex either, so a two-sided reading packet needs the manual flip.

Ownership is the easiest in this lineup. There are no nozzles to clog, so leaving it unplugged over winter break does no harm. Keep the starter toner in mind, because it runs out sooner than a full cartridge, and buy the replacement before finals week rather than during it. A stack of paper and a USB cable in the same drawer makes the setup complete, and the printer needs no more attention than a stapler.
products.bestFor: Students who print mostly black text and want the lowest cost per page.
pros: Toner does not dry out over breaks
Compact body fits a dorm desk
Mobile app prints from a phone
Low cost per page for essays

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 4-in-1 Wireless Inkjet with ADF
products.description:
Canon's TR4720 is the student desk workhorse: it prints in color, scans and copies with an automatic document feeder, and it sips 0.8 watts in standby so it will not bother a dorm electricity budget. The feeder is handy for scanning a pile of lecture handouts or signed forms.

The weak spot is ink. As a cartridge inkjet it costs more per page than a laser, so a student who prints hundreds of black pages a semester pays for it. The two-cartridge design also means an empty color cartridge ends color printing, which is why the Brother HL-L2405W is the cheaper choice for text.

Ownership requires a weekly test page so the printhead does not dry during a slow week. Setup runs through Canon's app and takes a few minutes. Treat the fax as unused hardware and focus on the scanner, which is the real reason to pick this model. When you move out, tape the scanner lid shut and pack the printer upright so the cartridges do not leak into the carriage.
products.bestFor: Students who need color, scanning and a feeder in one small unit.
pros: Color printing for posters and lab reports
Feeder scans stacks of handouts
Low standby power in a dorm
Phone setup through Canon's app
cons: Cartridge ink costs more per page
Needs weekly use to avoid clogs

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS4320 Wireless Inkjet All-in-One
products.description:
The TS4320 is Canon's affordable all-in-one, a printer that fits the budget of a first-year student. The listing describes two-cartridge printing for documents and photos, and setup from a phone or computer is quick enough for move-in day.

The tradeoff is running cost. A cartridge inkjet is cheap to own but costly to feed, and the single color cartridge empties fast on color-heavy classes. It lacks the Canon TR4720's feeder, so scanning a stack means lifting the lid repeatedly.

For ownership, keep a spare black cartridge since essays use it fastest, and print a page every week or two. Because it is light, it travels in a car trunk without drama. For a student who prints modestly, it covers the basics at a low entry cost. Pair it with a phone scanning app for receipts and you will rarely miss the feeder. If your major turns color heavy, upgrade to a tank rather than feeding this machine expensive cartridges.
products.bestFor: First-year students who need color and a scanner on a small budget.
pros: Low entry cost for a Wi-Fi all-in-one
Simple phone setup for move-in day
Light enough to carry between dorms
Print, scan and copy in one body
cons: Ink cost per page is high

products.name: HP DeskJet 2955 Wireless All-in-One Inkjet
products.description:
HP's DeskJet 2955 is the cheapest way to own a color printer here, aimed at to-do lists, letters and forms with a 60-sheet tray. It prints from a phone over Wi-Fi and scans and copies single pages.

A real limit is capacity and speed. A 60-sheet tray needs reloading on a long paper, and there is no duplex, so a thirty page document means thirty sheets. It suits a student who prints a few pages a week, not one who prints daily.

Ownership centers on the small cartridges, which empty fast. Buy a spare set, print weekly and read the terms on any ink subscription before enrolling. As a printer to keep in a drawer for the occasional form, it does the job. It also makes a reasonable hand-me-down: when you graduate, wipe the glass, pack the cartridges separately and it will serve a younger sibling or a first apartment.
products.bestFor: Students who print a handful of pages a week and want the lowest outlay.
pros: Lowest cost of the color printers here
Phone printing over Wi-Fi
Light and easy to carry
Scan and copy included

products.name: Brother Work Smart 1360 Wireless Duplex Inkjet
products.description:
Brother's Work Smart 1360 gives a student two things most dorm printers lack: automatic duplex and a 20-sheet feeder. Cloud connections let you scan a form straight to Google Drive or print from it, which helps when a laptop is out of reach.

The tradeoff is a higher tier than the entry inkjets and the usual cartridge cost. It is also heavier than the HP DeskJet 2955, so carrying it up three flights of stairs takes effort. For a student who writes long papers, duplex halves the paper bill.

Ownership follows the inkjet routine: weekly printing and a spare cartridge set. Brother's drivers are straightforward and the app handles setup. It suits a student who treats the printer as a long-term companion through four years. The cloud scan feature is the sleeper benefit, because a signed form can go straight to a Drive folder and then to an advisor without touching a laptop.
products.bestFor: Students who print long papers and want duplex and a feeder.
pros: Automatic duplex halves paper on long papers
20-sheet feeder scans short stacks
Cloud scanning and printing on the unit
Straightforward Brother drivers
cons: Heavier to carry on moving day
Cartridge cost per page remains high

products.name: Canon MegaTank G3270 Wireless Ink Tank All-in-One

specList.label: Ink in box
specList.value: Up to two years of ink

products.description:
Canon's MegaTank G3270 is the long-term cost play for a student: it ships with up to two years of ink and a yield of up to 6,000 black and 7,700 color pages per set. A student who prints a lot of color for design or science classes will spend little on ink for years.

The tradeoff is the higher entry price and the need for regular use. A tank printer left unplugged all summer can clog, so it is a poor fit for a student who stores the printer for months. It is also bulkier than a laser, which matters in a small dorm.

Ownership means printing something every week or two and refilling carefully from the bottle. If you will keep one printer through four years and print steadily, the savings add up. If your printing comes in bursts with long gaps, the Brother HL-L2405W is safer. Keep the ink bottles upright in a drawer and never store them in a hot car, because heat and tilt are how bottles leak and cap seals fail.
products.bestFor: Students who print color often and will keep one printer for years.
pros: Up to two years of ink in the box
Up to 7,700 color pages per ink set
Low cost per page for color
Scan and copy included
cons: Higher entry price than other options
Can clog if stored for months

buyingCriteria.explanation: A student prints mostly black text, and laser toner is the cheapest source of black pages. The Brother HL-L2405W costs less per page than any cartridge inkjet here, while the Canon TR4720 and HP DeskJet 2955 cost more. Compare replacement toner or ink yield, not the box price.

A printer is carried into a dorm and back out at the end of each year. The HP DeskJet 2955 and Brother HL-L2405W are light and compact, while the Brother Work Smart 1360 and Canon G3270 are heavier. Choose one you can carry in one trip.

Some dorm and campus Wi-Fi networks isolate devices, so a wireless printer may not be reachable from a laptop. A USB port is the fallback, and some printers offer a direct phone connection. Check the listing for USB before you buy.

Inkjet heads dry out if the printer sits for months, while laser toner does not. The Brother HL-L2405W survives a summer in a closet, but the Canon G3270 and the cartridge inkjets want a weekly page. If you store the printer between semesters, favor a laser.
Duplex halves paper for long papers, and the Brother Work Smart 1360 has it. A 60-sheet tray like the HP DeskJet 2955 runs out on a long job. Match both to the longest paper you write.

Students scan signed forms, receipts and lecture notes. A feeder on the Canon TR4720 or Brother Work Smart 1360 handles stacks, but a phone scanning app covers occasional pages. Pay for a scanner only if you will use it.

howWeEvaluated.title: Student cost
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared running cost, from laser toner on the Brother HL-L2405W to the ink tank economics of the Canon G3270. Cost per page for black text drove the ranking. Starter supplies were noted.

howWeEvaluated.title: Portability
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered weight and footprint, favoring the compact HP DeskJet 2955 and Brother HL-L2405W for dorm moves. Heavier units lost points for stairs. Cord and tray design were noted.

howWeEvaluated.title: Dorm network fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at wireless options and USB fallback, since campus networks can block printers. Phone setup and cloud features counted. A wired fallback is a safeguard.

howWeEvaluated.title: Idle tolerance
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed how each printer handles a summer in storage. Laser toner tolerates it, while inkjets and tanks need weekly use. The Brother HL-L2405W earned credit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Paper and scan features
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked duplex, tray size and feeders, with the Brother Work Smart 1360 and Canon TR4720 leading. Features students rarely use were not rewarded.

cards.label: Laser
cards.text: A laser like the Brother HL-L2405W costs little per page and survives summers in storage. It prints black only and has no scanner.

cards.label: Inkjet
cards.text: An inkjet like the Canon TR4720 prints color and scans, but ink costs more per page and nozzles need weekly use.

howToChoose.note: Pick a laser if your work is black text; pick an inkjet if you need color and a scanner.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Group projects mean posters, handouts and quick copies. Color and a scanner matter, along with a printer that wakes fast when a teammate arrives with a flash drive.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Canon TR4720 and Brother Work Smart 1360 fit best, one for its feeder and the other for duplex and cloud scanning.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more if you print weekly for four years, where the Canon G3270 saves on ink, or if you print long papers and want duplex from the Brother Work Smart 1360.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save if you print a few pages a week, where the HP DeskJet 2955 or Brother HL-L2405W covers the basics.

maintenance.why: Keeps nozzles wet. A short color page is enough.
A laser can sit sealed in a box. An inkjet should be used once a month or have its heads capped.
Essays use black fastest, and finals week is no time to wait for a delivery.
Dorm humidity curls paper and causes jams. Store the ream sealed.
Dust shows as lines on scans. Use a dry microfiber cloth.

faq.q: Is it cheaper to buy a printer or use the library?
faq.a: If you print under a few dozen pages a semester, the library is cheaper. Past that, a printer pays back, and a laser has the lowest cost per page for essays.

faq.q: Which printer is best for a dorm room?
faq.a: A compact laser such as the Brother HL-L2405W or a light inkjet like the HP DeskJet 2955 fits a small desk. Check the dorm rules and keep a USB cable handy.

faq.q: Will my printer work on campus Wi-Fi?
faq.a: Not always, because some campus networks isolate devices. A USB connection or a direct phone link is the reliable fallback.

faq.q: Is an ink tank worth it for a student?
faq.a: Yes if you print color weekly and keep the printer for years, because ink cost per page is low. If you store it over summers, a laser is safer.

A phone scanning app handles occasional pages. A feeder on the Canon TR4720 is worth it if you scan stacks of forms or notes. For one signed page a month, a free app and a flat surface beat paying for scanner hardware, and a laser without a scanner stays smaller and cheaper.

faq.q: How do I keep a printer alive over summer break?
faq.a: Store a laser dry and capped. For an inkjet or tank, print a page before you leave and again when you return, and keep the heads covered.
